questions.solution:

The numbers are 21, 63, and 105

**Calculation:**

42 = 2 × 3 × 7

63 = 3² × 7

105 = 3 × 5 × 7

Common prime factors from the given three numbers are 3 and 7

So, H.C.F = 3 × 7

⇒ 21

**∴ The required answer is 21.**

questions.question: An element with an atomic number of 17 is:

__
 
• **The halogens are referred to as group 7A or group 17 elements and are non-metals. **

 
 
• The halogens available are **Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I), and Astatine (At).** They are very reactive.
 
 
 
• **The element in the periodic table with an atomic number 17 is Chlorine and its symbol is Cl. Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
• Chlorine is used as a bleach in the manufacture of paper and cloth, pesticides, rubber etc.

• Elements partially filled with d orbitals are called **transition metals** and they can be located from group 3 to group 7.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true for the reaction of Calcium with water?

__
 
• **Calcium (Ca) is an alkaline earth metal in Group 2a** of the periodic table and the most abundant metallic element in the human body.
 
• Metals react with water produce metal oxide and release hydrogen gas.
 
• When Calcium reacts with water (H₂O), Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂) is formed along with the Hydrogen gas (H₂).
 
 
• **Ca₍ₛₒₗᵢd₎ + 2H₂O₍ₗᵢqᵤᵢd₎ → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂ ₍gₐₛ₎**
 
 
 
• **Calcium reacts slowly with water less vigorously and the heat evolved is less for the hydrogen formed to catch fire. Hence option 2 is correct.**

__
 
• In this reaction,** Calcium starts floating because the bubbles of Hydrogen (H₂) gas formed stick to the surface of the metal.**
 
• When water contains too much calcium or magnesium, it is called Hard water.

• In this reaction, CaO and Water are reacted to form a single product (Slaked lime) and the reaction where **one product is formed from two or more reactants is known as a Combination reaction.**

questions.question: Two balls of steel having mass of 5 kg and 10 kg each possess equal kinetic energy. Which ball is moving faster, if at all?

options.text: The 10 kg ball is moving faster.
Both the balls are moving at the same speed.
Kinetic energy does not depend upon the speed of the body.
The 5 kg ball is moving faster.

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Kinetic energy:

The energy possessed by a body by the virtue of its motion is called kinetic energy.

The expression for kinetic energy is given by:

K.E. = (1)/(2)m{V²}

where m₁ and m₂ are the mass of the 5 kg and 10 kg balls, and V₁ and V₂ are the velocities of the 5 kg and 10 kg balls, respectively. respectively. 

__Calculation:__

__Given:__

Since both balls have equal kinetic energy, we can set their kinetic energy expressions equal to each other:

 (1)/(2)m₁{V₁²}= (1)/(2)m₂{V₂²}

Rightarrow (1)/(2)×5times{V₁²}= (1)/(2)×10times{V₂²}

Rightarrow V₁²=2times V₂²

therefore V₁=sqrt{2}times V₂

This shows that the velocity of the 5 kg ball is the square root of two times greater than that of the 10 kg ball. **Therefore, the 5 kg ball is moving faster than the 10 kg ball.**

questions.question: Who coined the phrase 'Survival of the Fittest'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Herbert Spencer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Herbert Spencer:

 
 
• He was an educational philosopher and sociologist who considered "nature" as the supreme power.
 
• He was the one who emphasized the use of problem-solving techniques in education.
 
• His educational philosophy focused on the principle of naturalism based on the assumption that nature represents the wholeness of reality.
 
• Nature, itself, is a total system that contains and explains all existence including human beings and human nature.
 
• He believed that the material and the physical world are governed by certain laws, and man, who is the creator of the material world, must submit to it. 
 
• He gave the famous term "survival of the fittest" which means that only the strongest people can conquer challenging circumstances in real life by using their knowledge, skills, and conscience.
 
• Through this statement, he wants to convey that the students learn self-discipline more from their personal experiences of nature rather than the punishments given by teachers.
 
 
 
• So, it is concluded that Herbert Spencer coined the famous term "survival of the fittest".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Darwin** is well-known for his theory of evolution by natural selection.
 
• This theory states that nature keeps evolving along with the physical characteristics of an individual.
 
• So, only those individuals will survive in the changed or evolved natural conditions which cast themselves according to the circumstances.
 
• His theory was the basis for the Herbert Spencer quote "survival for the fittest".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He laid the foundation of mathematics in genetic science, known as Mendelism.
 
• Mendel used a number of contrasting visible characters of garden peas.
 
• Which includes round/wrinkled seeds, tall/short plants, white/violet flowers, etc.
 
 
 
• Har Gobind Khorana was an Indian American biochemist.
 
 
• He shared the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine in 1968.

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 32 and 48 hours, respectively. Pipe C can drain the entire cistern in 64 hours when no other pipe is in operation. Initially, when the cistern was empty Pipe A and Pipe C were turned on. After a few hours, Pipe A was turned off and Pipe B was turned on instantly. In all it took 112 hours to fill the cistern. For how many hours was Pipe B turned on?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 32 and 48 hours, respectively. Pipe C can drain the entire cistern in 64 hours when no other pipe is in operation.

**Concept used:**

Total work = LCM of time taken by the pipes to complete the task

**Calculation:**

Let the total amount of work be 192 units (L.C.M of 32, 48, and 64)

Amount of work done by pipe A in one hour = 192/32 = 6 units

Amount of work done by pipe B in one hour = 192/48 = 4 units

Amount of work done by pipe C in one hour = -192/64 = - 3 units

Let Pipe A and Pipe C operate for x hours.

After x hours, Pipe A is turned off and Pipe B is turned on. Now Pipe B and Pipe C will operate for the remaining 112 – x hours.

Work done by Pipe A and C in x hours = (6 – 3) × x units

Work done by Pipe B and C in (112 – x) hours = (4 – 3) × (112 – x) units.

The total work done should be 192 units.

So,

(6 – 3) × x + (4 – 3) × (112 – x) = 192

⇒ 3x + 112 – x = 192

⇒ 2x = 80

⇒ x = 40

So, Pipe B was turned on for 112 – 40 = 72 hours.

**∴ The required answer is 72 hours.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a task together in 35 days. If A works alone and completes (5)/(7) of the task and then leaves the rest for B to complete by herself, it will take a total of 90 days to complete the task. How many days would it take A, the more efficient among the duo, to complete the entire work by herself?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B can complete a task together in 35 days.

Total time taken is 90 days.

**Calculation:**

Let the total amount of work be 35 units.

If A and B work together, they complete 35/35 = 1 unit of work every day.

Now,

Let the amount of work done by A by himself in one day be x units and the work done by B by himself in one day be y units.

So, x + y = 1

If A works alone and completes 5/7th of the task,

work done by A is (5/7) × 35 = 25 units.

⇒ time taken by A to complete this 25 units of work = 25/x days.

If B works alone and completes 2/7th of the task,

work done by B is (2/7) × 35 = 10 units.

⇒ Time taken by B to complete this 10 units of work = 10/y days.

According to the question,

25/x + 10/y = 90

⇒ (25 + 10)/xy = 90

⇒ 25y + 10x = 90xy

⇒ 25(1 – x) + 10x = 90xy

⇒ 25 – 25x + 10x = 90x(1 – x)

⇒ 25 – 15x = 90x – 90x²

⇒ 90x² – 105x + 25 = 0

⇒ 18x² – 21x + 5 = 0

⇒ 18x² – 15x – 6x + 5 = 0

⇒ 3x(6x – 5) – 1(6x – 5) = 0

⇒ (6x – 5)(3x – 1) = 0

So, x = 5/6 (x cannot be 1/3 as A is more efficient among two)

Time taken by A alone to complete work by herself = 35/(5/6)

⇒ 42 days

**∴ The required answer is 42 days.**

questions.question: 15 pipes, each having the same diameter, can fill a cistern in 12 minutes. How long will it take for 6 pipes, each with double the original diameter, to fill the same cistern at the same speed of the flow?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The efficiency (flow rate) of a pipe is directly proportional to the square of its diameter.

Since the new pipes have double the diameter, their efficiency is 2² = 4 times that of the original pipes.

Total capacity of the cistern = 15 pipes × 1 unit × 12 minutes = 180 units.

Total efficiency of 6 new pipes = 6 × 4 units = 24 units/minute.

Time required = Total capacity ÷ New efficiency = 180 ÷ 24 = 7.5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Number of original pipes = 15

⇒ Time taken by original pipes = 12 minutes

⇒ Number of new pipes = 6

⇒ Diameter of new pipes = 2 × Original diameter

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Flow Rate (Efficiency) ∝ (Diameter)²

⇒ Total Work = Number of Pipes × Efficiency per pipe × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/932f4c52110ff3718fabaf3fcedb9af321ea107f4e7945501c568f288e16fff5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of 1 original pipe be 1 unit/min.

⇒ The new pipe has twice the original diameter, so its cross-sectional area and efficiency become 2² = 4 units/min.

⇒ Total combined efficiency of 15 original pipes = 15 × 1 = 15 units/min.

⇒ Total capacity of the cistern = Total original efficiency × Time taken = 15 × 12 = 180 units.

⇒ Total combined efficiency of 6 new pipes = 6 × 4 = 24 units/min.

⇒ Time required by new pipes = Total Capacity ÷ Combined New Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 180 ÷ 24 = 7.5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Flow Rule

When the speed of the fluid is constant, the volume of liquid flowing out is strictly proportional to the cross-sectional area of the pipe. Hence, Flow Rate ∝ r² or d².

MDH Work Equivalence Formula

Total work remains constant and can be solved using the chain rule: M₁ × D₁ × E₁ = M₂ × D₂ × E₂, where M is the number of pipes, D is the time elapsed, and E is the specific flow efficiency.

Rate & Efficiency Trick

If a pipe's radius or diameter is scaled by a factor of 'k', its filling capacity per unit of time scales by a factor of 'k²'. Time needed will correspondingly reduce by a factor of 'k²' for a single pipe.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is divisible by 6?

**Concept Used:**

We check the divisibility of 2 and 3.

The number which is divisible by 2 and 3 simultaneously will be divisible by 6.

Divisibility of 2: The number must end with 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.

Divisibility of 3: Sum of all digits of the given number should be divisible by 3

**Calculation: **

34672 : Last digit is 2 so divisible by 2 but sum of digits (3 + 4 + 6 + 7 + 2 = 22) is not divisible by 3, so number is not divisible by 6.

45678 : Last digit is 8 so divisible by 2 but sum of digits (4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 = 30) is divisible by 3, so number is divisible by 6.

23456 : Last digit is 6 so divisible by 2 but sum of digits (2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20) is not divisible by 3, so number is not divisible by 6.

56792 : Last digit is 2 so divisible by 2 but sum of digits (5 + 6 + 7 + 9 + 2 = 29) is not divisible by 3, so number is not divisible by 6.

**∴ 45678 is the number that is divisible by 6.**
